label: Fewer False Alarms On Embedded Forms
desc: The external form action check flagged any form posting to an absolute URL, including your own site written out in full and the newsletter or contact forms that Mailchimp, HubSpot, Jotform, Formspree, Salesforce and similar services tell you to embed. Those are now recognised and left alone, so an ordinary marketing page no longer collects a page of warnings for doing exactly what the vendor documented. Forms posting to a genuinely unknown domain are still reported, and a form posting over plain HTTP is now called out separately as the cleartext problem it actually is.

label: Secrets Hidden Behind An Example No Longer Missed
desc: Several secret checks looked at only the first match on a page before deciding whether it was a real credential or a documentation placeholder. If a page showed a sample token near the top, a genuine leaked one further down was never reported. Bearer tokens, AWS keys, GitHub tokens, database connection strings, reflected script payloads and clipboard-hijacking scripts are now each judged individually, so a placeholder can no longer hide a real finding behind it.

label: Clearer Stripe Key Finding
desc: The Stripe key finding was titled and worded as though any Stripe key in your page were a leak, while its own fix advice said publishable keys are safe in browsers. It only ever reports secret keys now, so the title, description and remediation steps say so plainly and tell you to roll the key and review recent account activity. Publishable keys, which Stripe requires you to put in client-side code, are no longer described as a payment risk.

label: postMessage Issue No Longer Counted Twice
desc: A page with a message listener that does not validate the sender's origin produced two separate high-severity findings for the same line of code, inflating the risk score. The weaker of the two duplicate checks has been retired, so the issue is reported once, by the version that inspects each listener individually instead of scanning the whole page.

label: Corrected Inline Iframe Finding Text
desc: The finding for an inline srcdoc iframe without a sandbox showed a fix instruction where the risk explanation should have been, and its remediation advised a sandbox setting that a different check flags as unsafe, because the two options together let framed content escape the sandbox entirely. The risk is now explained properly and the fix steps recommend the restrictive setting first, adding permissions back only where genuinely needed.
